description:
FILED s473t1 (Opus, the 13-file early-stop triage).  Bookkeeping, not a
compiler bug -- but it is 9 rows of `baselines/row-shortfall.tsv` that no fix
can ever remove, so it must be written down or it stays UNEXPLAINED forever.

MEASURED by running each file under REAL perl 5.40.3 (from the perl build
root, so `require "./test.pl"` finds perl's own test.pl):

  perl-tests/bop.t     plan tests => 510, real perl runs 509
      ("Looks like you planned 510 tests but ran 509")
      cause: session 245 commented out the `pack "P"` block (pointer pack,
      not supported) and left the plan.  PCL also runs 509 -- ZERO rows lost.
  perl-tests/eval.t    plan(tests => 169), real perl runs 163
      cause: the `${^MAX_NESTED_EVAL_BEGIN_BLOCKS}` block (perl 5.38+) is
      commented out; 6 assertions.  PCL produces the same 162 COUNTABLE rows
      perl does (the 163rd is `ok ` with no number -- eval.t:48 prints
      "ok $curr_test" with an empty variable, in real perl too).
  perl-tests/method.t  plan(tests => 163), real perl runs 161
      cause: session 245 commented out the two `"3foo"->CORE::uc` rows.

TO FIX: adjust the three plan counts to what the edited files actually
contain, in the same commit as a note in each file saying why.  That is an
edit to a perl-tests/*.t file, so it needs the USER's ruling (CLAUDE.md rule
5) -- the alternative is to restore the commented-out tests, which is a
different (and larger) question per block.

=== USER DECISION (s474b, 2026-09-07) ===
USER: "Let the bad counts be, as per your recommendation."  The three `plan` counts in perl-tests/bop.t, eval.t and method.t stay as they are; the 9 rows stay in baselines/row-shortfall.tsv with their s473t1 cause (`STALE PLAN, not a lost row`), which is the written-down explanation the shortfall bucket needs.  No file edited.  Closed as decided, not fixed.
subject: Three perl-tests files have a STALE `plan` -- a PCL edit commented tests out and left the count: bop.t +1, eval.t +6, method.t +2 rows of permanent shortfall
